Patchwork runs through the control-plane API with the scripted agent; questions are answered and deploys approved instantly by the harness, so repair times exclude human think time.
The baseline script was written once by a fresh Claude session from bench/baseline_prompt.md (recording, intent, v1 APIs, six sample messages) and is unchanged since.

Baseline Break 2 is measured on a fresh stack with contract v1, so Break 1 (which the script cannot repair) does not mask it. Sequentially the result is the same: the new sender is filtered out before any write.

per_record_min.note: Estimate, not timed: open the message, read PO/SKU/qty, switch to the Stockroom, pick the product from a 50-item list, type qty, paste the reference, save: ~45-60 s per record for a practised person. Replace with `python -m bench.stopwatch manual` (time 5, extrapolate).

per_record_min.source: Abhyankar, Qi, Zhang, 'OSWorld-Human: Benchmarking the Efficiency of Computer-Use Agents', arXiv:2506.16042 (v2, 2026): agents take 'tens of minutes' for tasks humans do in 'a few minutes', and the best agents take 2.7-4.3x more steps than necessary; latency is dominated by model calls
per_record_min.note: Estimate, not run (no computer-use API key): this is a ~1 min human task of ~15 GUI steps; at the cited 2.7-4.3x step overhead and several seconds per model-call step, ~3 min per record. Replace with `python -m bench.stopwatch computer_use` (run 5, extrapolate).
